clusters.mechanism: Exceptions thrown by classifyCi escape record() in the poller and abort the repository's observation loop, starving later PRs on every poll.
Repository slug/URL comparison is case-sensitive, so canonical-cased GitHub check_run_url values reject valid jobs and reruns.
The main-red branch continues before recording a CiFailure, so those failures never enter the flake ledger.
Rerun reconciliation searches only the workflow's latest attempt, so a later sibling-only attempt hides the originating job's result and throws Ambiguous CI rerun job.
Completed rerun jobs with skipped/neutral conclusions are never resolved and remain rerunning forever.
Main's legacy commit statuses are fetched only when the PR has status contexts or is truncated, hiding a failing main status with the same name as the PR's check.
Security-test exclusion is incomplete: whole-job or dependent-job reruns re-execute security tests because only failed steps or the selected job are checked.
The anchored timeout regex misses test timeout messages like Node's 'test timed out', so transient timeouts are classified as needing a fix.
A rerun claimed before the POST is never resolved when GitHub definitively rejects the request, leaving rerun_requested indefinitely.
The feed excerpt is the head of the raw job log (runner preamble) rather than the failing output.
The failure signature takes the first loosely matching error/fail line, which may be setup noise and includes volatile data such as durations, so signatures are unstable.
The change greatly exceeds the requested size budget and is overcomplicated, including a redundant second migration altering a table created in the same change.
Pre-existing restart-repair test in pipeline.test.ts fails on both base and HEAD, unrelated to this change.
A main-red pause leaves ciPending true so the REST inspection is repeated every poll even when GraphQL state is unchanged, wasting REST budget.
